title: Storebuilder Blueprint | Google for Developers
snippet:
Your Google Ads API developer token has multiple access levels. [Access Levels & Permissible Use](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/docs/access-levels) provides an overview about these access levels. To summarize:
- [Test account access](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/docs/access-levels#test_account_access): Execute up to 15,000 operations and make up to 1,000 requests per day using only test accounts. Once you complete the [Google Ads API sign up](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/docs/first-call/overview), you are issued a developer token set to this level. See the [test account guide](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/docs/first-call/overview#test_account) to learn more about how to create a test account.
- [Basic access](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/docs/access-levels#basic_access): Execute up to 15,000 operations and make up to 1,000 requests per day using test and production accounts. This is the default access level for all approved developer tokens. Production accounts are any accounts that serve real, live Google ads (test accounts don't serve ads). To apply, see [Applying for Basic access](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/docs/access-levels#applying_for_basic_access).
- [Standard access](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/docs/access-levels#standard_access): Execute unlimited operations and up to 1,000 requests per day using test and production accounts. For details of limits and exceptions, see [API quotas](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/docs/best-practices/quotas). If you have basic access level and you would like to apply for unlimited Google Ads API operations, fill out the [standard access application form](https://www.google.com/appserve/fb/forms/standardaccess/).
This form asks you detailed questions about the design of your software that uses the API, and also asks for design documents of your software. Note that "MCC" in this application refers to the Google Ads manager account.
Most partners need the Standard access level to scale their solution. The recommended approach is to gain Basic access during early development and testing. Then, a few weeks before you release your Performance Max integration into production, you would apply for Standard access and demonstrate that you meet the requirements for it (see next section).

title: developers.google.com/google-ads/api/docs/api-policy/access-levels.md.txt
snippet:
Permissible use only applies to Google Cloud projects with Standard access
level. Permissible use is allocated based on intended use of the Google Ads API. These
permissions determine which features of the API your tool can use, as
elaborated in the following table:
| Permissible Use | Description |
|---|---|
| Ad creation / management | Provide access to all services of the API for creating and managing Google Ads campaigns, ad groups, ads, and keywords. |
| Reporting | Only make [`GoogleAdsService.Search`](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/reference/rpc/v26/GoogleAdsService/Search) or [`GoogleAdsService.SearchStream`](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/reference/rpc/v26/GoogleAdsService/SearchStream) requests, or read-only calls. This is for developers who only use the API to request stats. |
| Researching keywords and recommendations | Allow the Google Cloud project to access [`RecommendationService`](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/reference/rpc/v26/RecommendationService), [`KeywordPlanIdeaService`](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/reference/rpc/v26/KeywordPlanIdeaService), and [`KeywordPlanService`](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/reference/rpc/v26/KeywordPlanService). This is only used by tools requiring suggestions to help facilitate the creation and management of Google Ads campaigns. |
### Change permissible use
If your Google Cloud project has been approved for Standard access level, you
can fill out the [application to update permissible use](https://support.google.com/adspolicy/contact/tool_change). Fill out
the application if you would like to update your permissible use or grant your
clients access to your tool.

title: Google Ads API comprehensive onboarding guide
snippet:
The developer token uniquely identifies your application to the Google Ads API and controls your call volume access tier.
### Steps to apply
1. Sign in to your **Google Ads Manager Account**.
2. Navigate to **Tools and settings > Setup > API Center** (or **Admin > API Center**).
3. Fill out the developer details form and agree to the API Terms of Service.
4. Submit your application.
### Access levels
- **Pending Approval:** Newly created tokens immediately receive a "Pending" status. You can use a pending token to connect to **Test Accounts** immediately, but it will not work against production accounts.
- **Basic Access:** Allows up to 15,000 API operations per day once approved.
- **Standard Access:** Unlimited daily API operations for applications that meet the Required Minimum Functionality (RMF).

### Pricing and billing note
- **No API Fees:** Creating a Google Cloud project, enabling the Google Ads API, and generating OAuth 2.0 credentials is **100% free**. Google does not charge any fees for calling or using the Google Ads API itself.

title: Developer token
snippet:
- A developer token is required to make calls to the Google Ads API and is a 22-character alphanumeric string obtained from the API Center page of your Google Ads manager account.
- Each developer token has an access level (Test, Basic, or Standard) which determines the number of API calls and the environment (test or production) it can be used in.
- Generally, a company only needs one developer token, but individual developers and companies creating new tools can apply for a new one if necessary.
- Both companies and individual developers can apply for a developer token, providing specific details during the application process.
- Applying for a developer token involves selecting or creating a Google Ads manager account and then completing the API Access form in the API Center.

### A new signup experience for the Google Ads API
You can [sign up for access to Google Ads API](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/docs/get-started/make-first-call#console-project) directly in the Google Cloud Console without requiring a Google Ads manager account. Don't sign up for a developer token from the [API Center page](https://ads.google.com/aw/apicenter) or attempt to apply for API access from the [API Center page](https://ads.google.com/aw/apicenter) in your Google Ads manager account as these processes have been transitioned to Google Cloud Console and won't be processed if initiated from the API Center page.

title: Access levels and RMF
snippet:
The Google Ads API has [access levels](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/docs/api-policy/access-levels) associated with the Google Cloud project, and uses an application review process to grant various access levels. It's important to plan and obtain the correct access levels before productionizing your application.

Google may require that your app provide certain capabilities or features as listed in the [Required Minimum Functionality (RMF)](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/docs/api-policy/rmf). When using the Google Ads API, the RMF only applies to Google Cloud projects with Standard access level. Make sure you review these requirements in advance to avoid additional delays around building the necessary features in your app.
## Pricing
The Google Ads API is free to use; there are no charges for using the Google Ads API at Explorer access, Basic access, or Standard access levels. However, if you are subject to [Required Minimum Functionality (RMF)](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/docs/api-policy/rmf), the API Review Team audits your tool for compliance. If the audit results in a finding of non-compliance, you may be required to pay [non-compliance fees](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/docs/api-policy/non-compliance-fee).
